{{Short description|Compact complex manifold in algebraic geometry}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''[[Boris Moishezon|Moishezon]] manifold''' {{mvar|M}} is a compact [[complex manifold]] such that the [[field (mathematics)|field]] of [[meromorphic function]]s on each component {{mvar|M}} has [[transcendence degree]] equal to the [[complex dimension]] of the component:

:<math>\dim_\mathbf{C}M=a(M)=\operatorname{tr.deg.}_\mathbf{C}\mathbf{C}(M).</math>

Complex [[algebraic variety|algebraic varieties]] have this property, but the converse is not true: [[Hironaka's example]] gives a smooth 3-dimensional Moishezon manifold that is not an algebraic variety or [[scheme (mathematics)|scheme]].  {{harvtxt|Moishezon|1967|loc=Chapter I, Theorem 11|authorlink=Boris Moishezon}} showed that a Moishezon manifold is a [[projective algebraic variety]] if and only if it admits a [[Kähler metric]]. {{harvtxt|Artin|1970}} showed that any Moishezon manifold carries an [[algebraic space]] structure; more precisely, the category of Moishezon spaces (similar to Moishezon manifolds, but are allowed to have singularities) is equivalent with the category of algebraic spaces that are proper over {{math|Spec('''C''')}}.
